overview.headline: Secret Philadelphia Convention drafted a new Constitution in summer 1787

keyPoints.point: delegates signed on September 17 1787 document which established government of United States
keyPoints.quote: signed on September 17, 1787, established the government of the United States

keyPoints.point: Federal Convention convened in Philadelphia on May 14 1787 to revise Articles of Confederation
keyPoints.quote: The Federal Convention convened in the State House (Independence Hall) in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787, to revise the Articles of Confederation.

keyPoints.point: members adjourned from day to day until quorum of seven states was obtained
keyPoints.quote: the members adjourned from day to day until a quorum of seven states was obtained on May 25

keyPoints.point: by mid-June it became clear Convention would draft entirely new frame of government rather than amend existing Articles
keyPoints.quote: it became clear by mid-June that, rather than amend the existing Articles, the Convention would draft an entirely new frame of government

keyTerms.gloss: assembly of delegates meeting in Philadelphia to debate and draft new plan of government
keyTerms.quote: Drafted in secret by delegates to the Constitutional Convention during the summer of 1787

keyTerms.gloss: minimum number of states required to be present to conduct business
keyTerms.quote: the members adjourned from day to day until a quorum of seven states was obtained on May 25

keyTerms.gloss: earlier system of government that Convention was called to revise
keyTerms.quote: The Federal Convention convened in the State House (Independence Hall) in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787, to revise the Articles of Confederation.

keyTerms.gloss: national power debated for allocation between Congress and states
keyTerms.quote: Among the chief points at issue were how much power to allow the central government, how many representatives in Congress to allow each state
